blocks.content: The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler is the automatic counterpart to the manual scaling covered in the Deployments module, watching a metric and adjusting replica count on its own, within bounds you define.

Where the Scaling topic in the Deployments module covered changing a replica count by hand, the HPA does exactly this automatically, continuously, based on real, observed demand rather than a manually chosen fixed number.

blocks.alt: The automatic version of the manual scaling covered back in the Deployments module

blocks.content:
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: my-app-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: my-app
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: cpu
        target:
          type: Utilization
          averageUtilization: 70

blocks.content: An HPA continuously watches a chosen metric, most commonly CPU utilization, but potentially memory or a custom application metric, and compares the current value against a target you specify.

blocks.alt: A continuous watch, comparing real demand against a chosen target

blocks.content: Scaling never runs unbounded, minReplicas and maxReplicas set a floor and a ceiling, the HPA is free to adjust anywhere within that range, but never below the minimum or above the maximum, regardless of what the metric says.

blocks.alt: A safe, defined range the automatic adjustment can never actually leave

blocks.content: An HPA is not limited to Deployments, it can target a Deployment, a bare ReplicaSet, or a StatefulSet, covered in their own modules, anything with a replica count the HPA can meaningfully adjust.

blocks.alt: Several workload types, anywhere a replica count genuinely makes sense to adjust

blocks.content: A real HPA watching CPU utilization, targeting 70%, between 2 and 10 replicas, will scale up automatically as traffic increases and demand pushes CPU usage higher, and scale back down once demand subsides, exactly the automatic responsiveness introduced back in the Why Kubernetes topic.

blocks.alt: Real, automatic responsiveness to actual, changing demand

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: The HPA automatically adjusts replica count based on a watched metric, the automatic counterpart to the manual scaling covered in the Deployments module.
minReplicas and maxReplicas keep automatic adjustment safely bounded, and an HPA can target Deployments, ReplicaSets, or StatefulSets alike.
